subject: Renewal: shortfall safety net + conditional price-hold proposal for MapleShop
messages:
From: Joe Martinez <joe@mapleshop.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion and shortfall protection request

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the pilot support earlier this year. We’re approaching our renewal and have a couple of asks from procurement that I wanted to put on the table before we get a draft SOW out. High level:

- Mapleshop wants a 12‑month price-hold on model unit pricing for any committed volume (to limit price volatility).
- We have some seasonality risk: procurement is asking for a shortfall safety net (credits if we under-utilize >20% against the commit during Q1).
- We’d like an option to increase committed capacity mid-term without penalty if we exceed 120% of forecast.

Can you share a proposal that includes discounts for a 12‑month commit, how the shortfall credits would work operationally, and whether the price-hold can be scoped to committed tiers (not bursts)? Procurement attached the RFP (see attached).

Quick call? We’re available Wed 21st afternoon.

Thanks —
Joe
Joe Martinez
Head of Platform Ops, MapleShop
joe@mapleshop.com

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Joe Martinez <joe@mapleshop.com>, Procurement <procurement@mapleshop.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion and shortfall protection request

Joe — thanks for the clear asks and the RFP. I’ve looped in Ben from pricing/ops so we can give numbers that align to capacity constraints.

High-level proposal (we’ll put formal numbers into the attached spreadsheet):

1) Commit + price-hold: 12‑month term with commitment tiers (50M / 100M / 200M tokens). For any tier you commit to, we can lock the model unit price for 12 months. That price‑hold applies to committed usage only, not to burst overage.

2) Shortfall safety net: If your quarterly committed usage is <80% of the committed tier, we provide a credit equal to 50% of the difference (i.e., a 50% shortfall credit) that rolls forward as account credit or applies to subsequent invoices in the term. The credit budget is capped at one quarter's worth of credits across the 12‑month term.

3) Upsize option: You can increase the committed tier once mid-term without penalty; we’d amortize any true‑up over remaining months.

Operational notes: credits will be issued as invoice line items with a shortfall calculation report from our billing/usage system. For auditability we’ll include monthly usage export.

I attached a draft proposal (redwood_proposal_v1.xlsx) with placeholders for price points. Can you confirm the target tier you have in mind and whether procurement prefers credits or refund?

I’m available Wed 21st 3pm PT for a quick 30m to walk through.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 415‑555‑0198

Attachment: redwood_proposal_v1.xlsx (xlsx stub)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MapleShop proposal — ops constraints and suggestion

Laura / Rishi — forwarding Joe’s note and Laura’s draft. A few operational caveats from infra/pricing:

- We can do the 12‑month price-hold for committed tiers, but for large commits (200M+) we need a minimal guaranteed burst pool reservation window so we don’t over-sell capacity in a region. That can be expressed as a soft reserved pool with 24‑48h notification for large bursts.
- Shortfall credit mechanics are fine, but recommend a 40–50% credit level and cap it at one quarter (agree with Laura). Also suggest credits are applied as account credit, not refunds, to keep accounting straightforward.
- For the upsizing option: allow one mid-term commit increase, but require a 30‑day notice for scheduling Dedicated capacity shifts; hosted customers can usually be upgraded faster.

I’ll add a small invoice timing concession (30‑day net to 45‑day net for the first invoice) to help procurement with cashflow.

-ben

Joe / Team — thanks for the call yesterday. Per discussion, attaching a clean termsheet (redwood_final_terms.docx) and a headline summary here for quick review.

Headline commercial (illustrative):
- Commit tier: 100M tokens / 12 months
- Effective unit price on commit (locked 12 months): $0.0025/token
- Shortfall credit: 45% of unused committed volume per quarter if usage <80%; credits issued as account credit and capped at 25M token equivalent over term
- Upsize: one mid-term upsize allowed; Hosted upgrades effective within 7 days, Dedicated require 30 days
- Invoice terms: 45 days for first invoice, 30 days thereafter

Operational attachments: redwood_final_terms.docx outlines reporting cadence (monthly usage export), credit calculation, and the fallback model variant list for capacity constraints.

Next steps: if procurement agrees to the headline, Laura — can you confirm we should route to Legal for an amendment (SOW + amendment) and start a DocuSign envelope? Proposed deal id: MAP-2027-087.
